entries.name: Age
entries: Celestials are much older than a lot of things in the universe maybe older than a few stars.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Celestial Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Radiant damage.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Celestial are generally curious about others but they don't have a standard alignment for all of them.

entries.name: Sacrifice Healing
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can sacrifice your life to heal others, you take {@damage 1d8}+{@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} irreducible Necrotic damage and you Heal a creature within 60ft. equal to the result.

entries.name: Sacrifice Protection
entries: When a creature that you can see within 60 ft. takes damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to redirect half of the damage before applying resistances or other reductions irreducible Necrotic damage. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Celestial Knowledge
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill History} and in the {@skill Religion} skills.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Celestial, and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Age
entries: Baccai are creatures modified by a failed ascension live a longer life than regular Humans, around 150 years.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Baccai are typically chaotic and usually evil.

entries.name: Knowledge of the old Times
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill History}, {@skill Religion} or {@skill Arcana} skills.

entries.name: Fragile Mind
entries: When you become {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} during a fight make a Wisdom saving throw (CD 10 plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}), on a failed save on your next turn you must use the {@action Attack|XPHB} most wounded creature other than yourself. This Attack is considered a {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can use either Dexterity or Strength for this attack. If you hit with them, you can deal slashing damage equal to double your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} bludgeoning damage, you heal a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage dealt.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Old Shuriman, and Modern Shuriman.

entries.name: Failed Tentative
entries: When you tried to ascend as a God-Warrior the ascension failed making you an Aberration during the process, choose one subrace option that determines the creature you have become.

entries.name: Sandmancy
entries: Your body has undergone a strange mutation. Your skin may shed grains of sand when scratched, appear covered in tiny specks like desert sand, and your wounds may release sand instead of blood. As you reach 5th and 11th level, these traits may become more pronounced, subject to the DM's approval.

entries.name: Sand Body
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can move through the space of any creature, though you can't willingly end your movement there. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saving throws made to end or escape the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Mobile Sands
entries: Starting at 5th level, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can surround yourself with an aura of shifting sand for 1 minute. The ground within 10 feet of you becomes covered in sand from your body and is {@quickref difficult terrain||3} for your enemies. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sand Absorption
entries: Starting at 11th level, when you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to halve the damage from that single source and immediately move up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. This movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Beast
entries: Your body develops aberrant bestial traits. Your face might resemble that of a desert beast, serpent-like scales may grow across your back, your eyes could become reptilian, or other unnatural appendages may emerge from your body. As you reach 5th and 11th level, these traits may become more pronounced, subject to the DM's approval.

entries.name: Natural Weapon
entries: You gain a natural weapon. When you hit with it, it deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier. When you create your character, choose whether this natural weapon deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, as appropriate to its form.

entries.name: Bestial Combat
entries: Starting at 5th level, when you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can make one attack with your natural weapon as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. In addition, your natural weapon deals extra damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Bestial Instinct
entries: Starting at 11th level, when you become {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} during combat, you can enter a state of bestial instinct for 1 minute. While in this state, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls you make with your natural weapon.
This state ends early if you regain enough {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to no longer be {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}.
Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Arcana
entries: Your body is infused with arcane energy. Your eyes may emit a faint blue, white, or orange glow. When you suffer slashing wounds, a soft radiance may be visible beneath the torn flesh instead of ordinary tissue. During moments of intense emotion, your hair may float weightlessly or even begin to fall away. As you reach 5th and 11th level, these traits may become more pronounced, subject to your DM's approval.

entries.name: Arcane Bolt
entries: You can unleash the arcane energy within you as a ranged attack with 60 feet of range. You use your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (chosen when you create your character) for the attack roll. If you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature, you can instead use your spellcasting ability modifier. On a hit, the attack deals {@damage 1d6} Force or Radiant damage (chosen when you create your character) plus the chosen ability modifier.

entries.name: Arcane Surge
entries: Starting at 5th level, when you hit a creature with your Arcane Bolt or with a spell, you can release a burst of residual magical energy. Each other creature within 10 feet of the target takes extra damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Arcane Flight
entries: Starting at 11th level, you can use a Bonus Action to gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB|Flying Speed} equal to your walking speed for 1 minute. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Age
entries: Vastaya can live to 500 years thanks to their spiritual lineage, but there are stories about some very old Vastaya that were deeply connected to the spiritual selves.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells.

entries.name: Wildborn
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Survival}. You are capable of a limited communication with animals of sorts, they are capable of comprehending what you say but you aren't capable of understanding them in return. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on charisma checks to influence them.

entries.name: Dreaming Awareness
entries: Your sylvan nature makes you alert while sleeping, you don't have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} during a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Sylvan, and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Riding the Wind
entries: Because of your wings, you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB|Flying Speed} equal to your walking speed. You can't use this {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB|Flying Speed} if you're wearing medium or heavy armor.

entries.name: Flying Combatant
entries: Starting at character level 5 you can fly while wearing medium or heavy armor.

entries.name: Agile Body
entries: You gain an extra 10 feet of walking speed, and your jump distance is doubled. Additionally, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to leap up to half of your remaining movement without provoking opportunity attacks.

entries.name: Evasive Leap
entries: Starting at character level 5 your reflexes allow you to evade danger before it strikes. When a creature makes a melee attack against you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to jump to an unoccupied space within half your maximum jump distance. The triggering attack is made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Ambush Predator
entries: You can attempt to Hide even when you are only {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB}. In addition, you develop precise natural weapons such as fangs, claws, or a tail. You can use these in place of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. These natural weapons deal {@damage 1d6} damage and can deal Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, as appropriate to their form.

entries.name: Silent Hunt
entries: Starting at character level 5 you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Stealth} checks you make to {@action Hide}.

entries.name: Mystic Feather
entries: You can pluck plumes from your body and transform them into {@item Mystic Feathers|Arcamis}. Whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action or make an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB}, you can manifest a Mystic Feather in your free hand and use it for that attack. The feather loses all magical properties immediately after it hits or misses a target.
The Mystic Feather has the following properties:

mastery.note: you can use this property, and it doesn't count against the number of properties you can use with Weapon Mastery

entries.name: Healer
entries: When you throw the feather, you can choose not to deal damage and instead restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to the target equal to the damage you would have dealt.

entries.name: Deadly Plumes
entries: Starting at character level 5 if you choose to use your feathers to deal damage, they don't count toward the number of uses of this feature.

entries.name: Highland Rescuer
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your walking speed, and you can move across vertical surfaces. Additionally, whenever you roll dice for features or spells that restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you treat any die roll of 1 as a 2.

entries.name: Vitality of the Peaks
entries: Starting at character level 5 as a {@action Magic|XPHB|Magic Action}, you can touch a creature, causing it to regain {@damage 1d6} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Inherent Glamour
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can shape-shift to change your appearance and your voice. You determine the specifics of the changes, including your coloration, hair length, and sex. You can also adjust your height and weight and can change your size between Medium and Small. You can make yourself appear as a member of another playable species, though none of your game statistics change. You can't duplicate the appearance of an individual you've never seen, and you must adopt a form that has the same basic arrangement of limbs that you have. This trait doesn't change your clothing and equipment. You stay in the new form until you take an action to revert to your true form.

entries.name: Glamour of Nature
entries: Starting at character level 5 you can assume the appearance of a creature or plant that you have seen at least once. You can alter your size to match the size of the creature or plant, up to a maximum size of Large. While transformed in this way, you have Advantage on Charisma ({@skill Deception} and {@skill Persuasion}) checks made to pass yourself off as that creature or plant.

entries.name: Robust Anatomy
entries: When you aren't wearing armor, your natural Armor Class becomes 12 + your Constitution modifier. You can still gain the benefits of a shield normally. Additionally, you are considered one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

entries.name: Overgrowth
entries: Starting at character level 5 your {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB} maximum increases by 5, and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level.

entries.name: Mystic Charm
entries: Mystical influence flows through your veins. Magic can't put you to sleep. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Performance}, or {@skill Persuasion}. Starting at character level 5 you gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the list above.

entries.name: Age
entries: Before being sealed by the Aspect of Targon, Darkin lived their lives and are at least 500 years old.

entries.name: Ascended Resilience
entries: When you take damage that would reduce you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can immediately regain one Hit Point. When you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blood Magic
entries: Darkin mastered the arcane power of blood magic, hemomancy. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you can use you blood magic to heal yourself for an amount equal to {@damage 1d6} + your Constitution modifier. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The quantity of healing received by this feature scales with your levels: {@damage 1d10} when you reach levels 5th level, {@damage 1d12} 10th level and {@damage 2d6} 17th level.

entries.name: Sealed Soul
entries: The Darkin were sealed within powerful objects. Choose one of the following item types. You gain proficiency with your chosen item and its Blood Enhancement.

A Darkin weapon grows in power through battle. Whenever you gain the required level, you can evolve your Darkin item by performing a ritual in a temple of Shurima and spending materials whose value equals the weapon's enhancement bonus (subject to the DM's discretion).

Your Darkin weapon has a number of charges equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded down). You regain all expended charges when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Activating a Blood Enhancement requires a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expends 1 charge.

entries.caption: Darkin Items
rows: All simple and martial melee weapons.

{@bold Laceration.} Spend 1 charge. Your next melee weapon attack gains +1 + your Darkin Weapon bonus to the attack roll. On a hit, up to two other creatures within your reach of the target each take damage equal to half the damage dealt by the attack.

{@bold Perforation.} Spend 1 charge. Your next ranged weapon attack gains +1 + your Darkin Weapon bonus to the attack roll. The attack pierces its target, and one creature directly behind it in the line of fire takes damage equal to half the damage dealt.

{@bold Aegis.} Spend 1 charge. Until the start of your next turn you gain +1 + your Darkin Weapon bonus to AC and regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to 3 + your Darkin Weapon bonus + your character level. The next time you take damage before this effect ends, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage except radiant damage for that instance of damage.
Arcane and druidic focus worth more than 1gp.

{@bold Infestation.} Spend 1 charge. The next spell you cast deals additional necrotic damage equal to twice your Darkin Weapon bonus. Choose one creature damaged by the spell or that fails its saving throw; it is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} until the end of your next turn. If that creature dies while affected, each creature within 10 feet of it (other than you) must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take necrotic damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and become {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Old Shuriman, and one language from the host.

entries.name: Age
entries: The ascension with the Sun Disc gave you a powerful body that can endure for centuries, God-Warriors can live for a very long time.

entries.name: Ascended Resilience
entries: When you take damage that would reduce you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can immediately regain one Hit Point. When you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Lords of the Desert
entries: When you are in the desert you can't be surprised, you have advantage on Wisdom checks ({@skill Survival}) and intelligence checks ({@skill Nature}) while you are in a desert. You aren't affected by negative effects caused by hot climate.
You obtain one of the following skill of your choice: {@skill Religion}, {@skill Survival} or {@skill Nature}.

entries.name: Ascension Form
entries: Your ascension gave you supernatural powers, these powers reflect your soul and body.

rows:
{@bold Predator of the Sun.} Once per turn when you hit a creature for the first time you can add {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage to the attack and you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
{@bold Battle Form.} You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to grant you the benefits of {@spell Enlarge/Reduce|XPHB}. You can do this action a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and you regain all expended uses at the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

{@bold Sun Wrath.} You can use the power of the Sun Disc. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you emit bright light in a 20-foot radius for 1 minute. For the duration or until you become {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} you add {@damage 1d4} radiant damage to your spell damage. Once you use this privilege you can't use it again until a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
{@bold Imperial Gaze.} You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice from {@skill intimidation} or {@skill persuasion}. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you can choose a creature within 30-feet that you can see. The creature must succeed a Wisdom Saving Throw DC = 10 + {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} or gains {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} at the first attack made in their next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and it recharges when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Old Shuriman, and one language from the host.

entries.name: Ascended Resilience
entries: When you take damage that would reduce you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can immediately regain one Hit Point. When you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Embodied Stars
entries: You have an innate connection to Mount Targon and its cosmic entities. When you are in mountainous or celestial environments, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Survival} checks made to navigate or avoid becoming lost.

entries.name: Blessing of an Aspect
entries: Climbing Mount Targon has convinced an Aspect to grant you a portion of its power. Choose one of the following blessings, or work with your DM to create a blessing of equivalent power.

rows: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can invoke your Aspect to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to yourself or one willing creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The creature regains {@dice 1d10} + your ability modifier {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

You have {@variantrule Darkvision|XPHB} out to a range of 60 feet. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can establish a telepathic link with one creature within 60 feet of yourself or one creature you have seen within the same day. You can communicate telepathically with that creature while you both share at least one language.
As an {@action Action|XPHB}, you can attempt to confuse the creature with nonsensical or rambling words. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next ability check or attack roll until the end of its next turn. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can enter a state of glorious starlight for 1 minute. The first time you hit with an attack on each of your turns, the attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Radiant damage. You emit {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius. Creatures within this radius can't benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, your body darkens as if covered in supernatural shadow for 1 minute. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks, and the first time you hit with an attack on each of your turns, the attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Versatile
entries: You gain proficiency in two of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Medicine} and {@skill Stealth}.

entries.name: Toxic Form
entries: You gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage.

entries.name: Seen Too Much
entries: You gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Good Stuff
entries: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift. Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can become two sizes larger, up to a maximum of Huge, for 1 minute, only if the surrounding environment allows it at the DM’s discretion. While transformed, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your {@skill Athletics} checks, you are immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, you gain a {@damage 1d4} bonus to attack rolls made with your weapons or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}, and the first attack you hit with on each turn deals extra damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. When this effect ends, you gain one level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} as the chemical substances leave your body.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Thieves' Cant, and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Magical Enhancements
entries: You can learn one {@filter cantrip from the Wizard spell list|spells|level=0|class=Wizard}. Choose Charisma, Wisdom, or Intelligence when you create your character. The chosen ability score is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip.

entries.name: Fortified Mind
entries: You gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Arcane Defenses
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one of the following damage types of your choice: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.

entries.name: Hextech Overload
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can activate the Hextech engines within you for 1 minute. While active, you gain a 10-foot bonus to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, gain a d4 bonus to attack rolls, and you can move normally through magical and nonmagical difficult terrain.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Piltovian, and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Spiritic Nature
entries: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Performance} or {@skill Nature}.

entries.name: See Through Veils
entries: You can sense what lies beyond the Material Plane. You can sense if there are creatures that are invisible or ethereal within 10-feet of you, you don't know the exact location of those creatures.

entries.name: Evanescent Body
entries: Your spiritual nature makes you easier to avoid material threats. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} for a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} you become partially ethereal until the start of your next turn (Moving through creatures' spaces doesn't count as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for you and {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}).

entries.name: Spiritual Legacy
entries: Your essence is infused with magic. You learn one {@filter cantrip from the Druid spell list|spells|level=0|class=Druid} of your choice that does not deal damage. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma when you gain this trait. The chosen ability score is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip.

entries.name: Becoming a Hag
entries:
Ionia is the land of balance, between Harmony and Torment, Life and Death. The Spirits of Ionia are no different. A spirit's nature can be Harmonious or Tormented. Important events, traumas, and their consequences can cause a Harmonious Spirit to become Tormented, or vice versa.

The Ionian Spirit must make a {@bold Wisdom Saving Throw} against a DC equal to 10 + half its {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded up). The character may choose to fail this {@bold Saving Throw}. On a failure, the Spirit changes its state. A Spirit can change its state only twice per week.

{@bold Harmonious to Tormented.} Events such as allies that the character cares about falling in battle, overwhelming feelings of sorrow, or deep resentment may force the Spirit into a state of Torment.

{@bold Tormented to Harmonious.} Joy, love, victory in battle, or finding peace may restore a Tormented Spirit. After witnessing significant events, the Spirit of Ionia may finally regain its long-sought tranquility.

entries.name: Harmonious Spirit
entries: {@bold Pacifying Presence.} As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can create a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that lasts for 1 minute. At the start of your turn for the duration, you and allied creatures within the emanation gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated}.

{@bold Hand of Balance.} When a creature within 20 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add or subtract {@damage 1d4} from the result. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Tormented Spirit
entries: {@bold Aggressive Presence.} As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you assume an aggressive form for 1 minute. Once per turn, when you hit a creature for the first time, you can add necrotic or psychic damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the first damage roll. This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.
{@bold Hunter of the Unnatural.} Your existence is bound to hunting creatures that do not come from the Material Plane. You gain {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} out to a range of 20 feet.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and two other languages of your choice.

entries.name: Bandle Cunning
entries: When you create your character, choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws using the chosen ability.

entries.name: Sudden Vanishing
entries: When you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to become {@condition Invisible} until the start of your next turn or until you attack, cast a spell, or deal damage. You can use this feature once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Yordle, and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Water Affinity
entries: Your walking speed is 30 feet, and you have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB|Swimming Speed} equal to your walking speed.

entries.name: Help from the Sea
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can summon a sea spirit at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The spirit briefly emerges in the form of a massive shark, ghostly fish, or another aquatic creature of your choice. Each creature within 5 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier). On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d6} Cold damage and is knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}. The damage increases by {@damage 1d6} at character levels 5, 11, and 17.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency Bonus|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Guerrilla Warfare
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill. If you already have proficiency with that skill, your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} is doubled for any ability check you make that uses it.

entries.name: Nature's Gift
entries: You know the {@spell Guidance|XPHB} and {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} cantrips.

entries.name: Spirit Magic
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can cast {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot. Starting at 3rd level, you can also cast {@spell Pass without Trace|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast these spells in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select this species).

entries.name: Technical Mind
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB}. In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill History}) and Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks related to mechanical devices or magic items.

entries.name: Unstable Gadgets
entries: During a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can create up to two of the following gadgets. a gadget stops functioning if you create another gadget beyond this limit. A creature can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to activate a gadget:

data.name: Snap Module
entries: When activated, the user gains a +10-foot bonus to their Speed and can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} until the end of their turn.

data.name: Scrap Shield
entries: When activated, the user gains {@dice 2d4} + the crafter's {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} temporary {@variantrule Hit Points}.

data.name: Explosive Projectile
entries: This gadget can be thrown up to 60 feet. It explodes in a 10-foot radius. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d10} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Void Resilience
entries: Your body has become an anomaly of matter.. When you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, your base AC is 12 + {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC.

entries.name: Killer Instinct
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can enter a state of insatiable hunger for 1 minute. While in this state, you gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Survivial Instinct
entries: If you have a free hand you gain a +2 bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}

entries.name: Void Hunger
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature for the first time, you add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the damage.

entries.name: Defensive Adaptation
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to psychic and poison damage. However, your unusual physiology is highly sensitive to vibrations. You have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to thunder damage, and you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws against effects that produce sound.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Quori, and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Artificial Nature
entries: You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in 4 hours if you spend those hours in an inactive, motionless state. During this time, you appear inert but remain conscious.

entries.name: Artisan Quality
entries: Your design may be unsettling, intricate, or welcoming. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Performance}, or {@skill Persuasion}.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and two other languages of your choice.

entries.name: Long Reach
entries: Thin strands extend from the joints of your limbs. During your turn, when you make an attack with a melee weapon that lacks the Reach, Two-Handed, and Versatile properties, that weapon has a reach of 10 feet for that attack.

entries.name: Hidden Threat
entries: You are indistinguishable from a porcelain doll until you strike. When you deal damage to a creature with a weapon attack during your first turn in combat, the creature takes extra damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. This additional damage is the same type as the weapon's damage.

entries.name: Core Barrier
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to redirect energy from your core toward it. The target gains a bonus to its {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} against that attack equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Soft Padding
entries: Your body is filled with soft cushioning. When you take bludgeoning damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage that triggered this reaction. In addition, you are pushed 5 feet away from the source of the damage. You can't use this reaction if there is no available space for you to be pushed.

{@italic Creatures born from the desires and vices of mortals}. Among the demons known to us are Evelynn, Agony's Embrace; Tahm Kench, the River King; Fiddlesticks, the Ancient Fear; and Nocturne, the Eternal Nightmare.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Demons Everywhere
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain a flying or swimming speed equal to your walking speed. To conceal your true nature, you can hide features such as your tail, gills, or wings by using a Bonus Action to assume the appearance of a Humanoid of your choice. You are considered a Shapechanger for the purpose of effects such as {@spell True Seeing|XPHB}.

entries.name: Child of Temptation
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} skill. When you attempt to convince a creature to perform an action that aligns with your vice, you can roll a {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to your {@skill Persuasion} check.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common, Infernal, and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Subspecies
entries: When you choose this species, choose one of the following subspecies. Also choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. The chosen ability is your spellcasting ability for spells granted by your subspecies and is used when calculating the save DCs of your subspecies features. At 3rd level, you gain the first trait of your chosen subspecies. At 5th level, you gain the second trait listed for that subspecies.

entries.name: The Art of Doing Nothing
entries: You always have the {@spell Slow|XPHB} prepared and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot, but when you do, it can target only one creature. You can regain this use if you spend a 2nd or higher level Spell Slot or when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

When a creature within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or dies, not by your actions, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your character level + your chosen ability modifier. You regain all expended uses after a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Suffocating Presence
entries: When a creature within 30 feet of you makes a saving throw against being {@bold Slowed} or has its Speed reduced by one of your effects, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose one of the following effects:

items: The creature can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn.
The creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next attack roll.
The creature's Speed becomes 0 until the end of its turn.

entries.name: Obsessive Desire

entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Investigation} skill.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB|Magic Action}, you choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your chosen ability modifier, chosen when you create your character). On a failed save, the creature develops an obsessive desire toward one visible object of your choice for 1 minute.

items: The creature considers that object extremely valuable.
The creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures possessing that object.
If the creature can reach the object using its movement, it must use part of its movement to move closer to it.
If the creature is holding the object, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against being {@bold Disarmed} or {@condition Grappled|XPHB}.

entries: The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Soul Collector
entries: When a creature affected by {@bold Obsessive Desire} dies, is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or willingly loses the desired object, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain one of the following benefits:

items: Gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level.
Gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your next attack roll or ability check.
Become {@condition Invisible|XPHB} to that creature until the end of your next turn.

entries: You can use {@bold Obsessive Desire} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Insatiable Appetite
entries: You can replace one attack on your turn with an attempt to swallow a creature your size or smaller. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, your jaws consume the creature, causing it to become {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB}. The creature is also considered to have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}.

As an action on your turn, you can deal a number of {@damage d6} of bludgeoning damage equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded down) to the swallowed creature and regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the damage dealt. You can regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} this way a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier.
You can swallow only one creature at a time, and you can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
Whenever you take damage, you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 10 + half the damage taken) or the effect ends.
The effect also ends if you take more than 20 damage from a single source or become {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, or {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.

entries.name: Voracious Adaptation
entries: Your body adapts to consume anything. While a creature is swallowed:

items: It automatically takes the damage from this feature at the start of your turn.
It can't regain Hit Points.
You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

entries: In addition, you can swallow creatures one size larger than you.
If a creature dies while swallowed, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your character level + your Constitution modifier.

entries.name: Otherworldly Envy
entries: You always have {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} prepared. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, and you can regain this use if you spend a 2nd or higher level Spell Slot or when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

While {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} is active, you can expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} to deeply probe the target's mind. The creature must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your chosen spellcasting ability modifier) or suffer one of the following effects:

items: {@b Resentment}. The first attack you make against the creature deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage.
{@b Aggression}. The creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom or Charisma ability checks made against you.
{@b Competition}. Choose one skill in which the target is proficient. You gain proficiency in that skill for the duration of the spell.

{@b Kleptomania}. Choose one object the target possesses. You learn its last location, and until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks made to steal it.

{@b Stalking}. Choose one creature the target considers friendly. You learn its last location, and until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks made to reach it.

entries: On a successful saving throw, the creature is immune to this feature for 24 hours. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Identity Theft
entries: When a creature fails the saving throw against your {@b Otherworldly Envy} feature, you can also gain one of the following additional benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against the creature.
You copy one of the creature's saving throw proficiencies.
You copy one of the creature's special movement speeds (swimming, climbing, or flying) for up to 10 minutes.
You copy one of the creature's tool proficiencies.

entries: You can have only one copied benefit at a time.

entries.name: Induce Rage
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Intimidation} skill.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB|Magic Action}, you can instill blind rage in creatures of your choice within 15 feet of you. Creatures of your choice within range must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your chosen ability modifier). On a failed save, a creature is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} until the end of its turn. While Charmed by this feature, it must use the weapon in its hand to attack the nearest creature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Frenzied Massacre
entries: When a creature fails the saving throw against your {@b Induce Rage} feature, it can immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a weapon attack against the nearest creature. In addition, when a creature within 30 feet of you is hit by a critical hit or is reduced below half its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can choose one creature affected by your {@b Induce Rage} feature. That creature gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its next attack roll, but attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Lustful Kiss
entries: You always have {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} prepared. You can cast it once at 1st level without expending a spell slot, and you regain this use when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you cast the spell or while it is active, you can expend up to half your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} to end the spell early, causing affected creatures to forget they were Charmed by you and marking one creature Charmed by the spell. The mark is invisible, emits an aura of Enchantment, and can only be seen by creatures with {@spell True Seeing|XPHB}. If the marked creature comes into contact with you or a creature you choose within the next 24 hours, it takes a number of {@damage d4} Necrotic damage equal to the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} spent + your spellcasting ability modifier. If this damage reduces the creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it becomes stable and {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} for {@damage 1d4} hours. You gain the same number as maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Vital Siphon
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB|Magic Action}, choose one creature within 20 feet of you. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier). On a failed save, you can expend up to two {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}, roll them, and add your Charisma modifier. The creature takes Necrotic damage equal to the result, and you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage dealt. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1), regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Superiority
entries: You always have {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB} prepared. You can cast it on yourself or a creature within 60 feet without requiring Somatic, Material, and Verbal components. The creature must also succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your chosen ability modifier) or become {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, seeing creatures around it as harmless and non-threatening.
You can cast it once without expending a spell slot and you can regain this use if you spend a 2nd or higher level Spell Slot or when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Divine Ego
entries: Your presence convinces others of your perfection. While a creature is affected by your {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, it gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} at the start of its turn and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against being {@condition Frightened|XPHB}. If the creature misses an attack roll or fails an ability check, it takes Psychic damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, as its confidence is shaken by failure.

entries.name: Darkin Rules
entries: A Darkin can possess only one host at a time and cannot bond with another creature while its current host lives.
If a Darkin loses its host, its consciousness remains trapped within its weapon until another creature attempts to wield it.
If a Darkin loses its host through violent destruction, it cannot bond with a new host for 100 years while its power recovers.

subclassFeature.name: Chemtechnician
entries: {@i Master Forcefields as a Tool for Protection}

Though often toxic, unstable, and explosive, chemtech combines machinery and chemical compounds to enhance its users beyond the limits of ordinary mortals. Skilled Chemtechnicians can harness chemical energy to create remarkable and deadly devices, even augmenting their own bodies to survive hostile environments or overcome physical limitations.

subclassFeature.name: Chemtechnician Spells
entries: When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Chemtechnician Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Chemtechnician Spells
rows: {@spell Melf's Acid Arrow|XPHB}, {@spell Wither and Bloom|SCC}

subclassFeature.name: Shimmer Distiller
entries: At 3rd level, you learn how to create a small alchemical drone powered by Shimmer-infused compounds. The drone floats around you, analyzing and modifying chemical substances to enhance your spells. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you create a {@creature Shimmer Drone|Arcamis}, and you can have only one drone at a time.

entries.name: Remote Casting
entries: You can cast spells as though you were in the drone's space, but you must use your own senses.

entries.name: Drone in Combat
entries: In combat, the drone shares your turn and acts immediately after you. It can move up to 60 feet on your turn without requiring an action. The only action it can take on its turn is {@action Dodge|XPHB}. If the drone moves more than 60 feet away from you, or if you become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, it enters standby mode, unless stated otherwise by another feature. While in standby mode, the drone is inactive and cannot take actions, move, or respond to commands. You can restore the drone by using the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

subclassFeature.name: Toxic Advancement
entries: You learn the {@spell Poison Spray|XPHB} cantrip. If you already know this cantrip, you can learn one other {@filter cantrip from the Artificer spell list|spells|level=0|class=Artificer} instead. Additionally, when you cast {@spell Poison Spray|XPHB}, you can cast it as a {@action Bonus Action|XPHB} instead of an {@action Action|XPHB}.
Additionally you gain the following features.

entries.name: Chemical Reserve
entries: Your drone adds your Intelligence modifier to the effects of its Chemical Diffuser and Chemical Synthesis traits.

entries.name: Shimmer Infusion
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can administer Shimmer to a creature through your drone. The creature must be within 10 feet of the drone. Until the end of the creature's next turn, it its Speed increases by 10 feet, has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, and its weapon and unarmed strikes deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage. At the end of its turn, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 10). On a failed save, it has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: High-Quality Shimmer
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you use your Shimmer Infusion feature, you can extend its duration to 1 minute for one creature. When you do so, your drone stays alongside that creature and gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks made to escape the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. The first time the creature drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} while under this effect, it enters a state of Frenzy instead of becoming {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. While in {@i Frenzy}, the creature remains at 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but can continue to act. If it takes damage equal to or exceeding its {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB} maximum, it dies from massive damage. While in {@i Frenzy}, the creature doesn't make {@variantrule Death Saving Throws|XPHB}. While the creature is in {@i Frenzy}, the damage dealt by Shimmer Infusion increases to {@damage 1d6}. Additionally, whenever the creature kills another creature, the drone performs a blood transfusion from the slain creature, restoring the Frenzied creature to 1 {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB}. Once this occurs, the effects of Shimmer Infusion and High-Quality Shimmer end.

subclassFeature.name: Shimmer Wave
entries: As an {@action Magic|XPHB|Magic Action}, you release a wave of Shimmer in a 30-foot line that is 15 feet wide, originating from yourself or your drone. Each creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw against your Artificer spell save DC. On a failed save, creatures are affected by your Shimmer Infusion feature as if you had used it on them and must immediately use their {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack against the nearest creature they can reach. These creatures act as if they were taking their turns for the purpose of this attack, using their abilities to the best of their ability. You can use this feature once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can use it again before finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} by expending a spell slot of 4th level or higher.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Frost
entries: Possessing a rare magical lineage passed down through generations of Freljordian barbarians, the Iceborn are naturally resistant to the cold and can wield True Ice and Black Ice without suffering pain or death. Though their origins trace back to a forgotten and ancient era, the Iceborn of today harness their inherited power to become unrivaled leaders and warriors of the Freljord.

subclassFeature.name: Ice Veins
entries: You can wield and wear weapons and armor made with {@b True Ice} or {@b Dark Ice} without side effects.
You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.
You can move through {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} caused by snow or ice without spending extra movement and you don't have side effects while being in {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG}.

subclassFeature.name: Iceborn Fury
entries: While you are raging, the first time you hit a creature with a weapon attack on each of your turns, that creature's Speed is reduced by 15 feet until the end of its turn.

subclassFeature.name: Blessing of True Ice
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one of the following objects to imbue with {@b True Ice}: a weapon you are wielding or a garment you are wearing. The chosen object gains the corresponding benefit until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Weapon
entries: When you deal damage with an attack using this weapon, you can change its damage type to Cold. Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with this weapon, you can use your {@action Bonus Action|XPHB} to freeze not only its flesh but also its soul. The target takes {@damage 1d10} Cold damage and can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Garment
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} conditions, as well as against effects that reduce your Speed. In addition, whenever a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, that creature takes Cold damage equal to your Constitution modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Shatter
entries: Your attack rolls with melee weapons and Unarmed Strikes against a creature whose Speed has been reduced by your Frostborn Rage feature can score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@damage d20}. This expanded critical hit range can't be increased by any other feature or effect.

subclassFeature.name: Legacy of the Iceborn
entries: When you enter your {@condition Rage|XPHB}, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Barbarian level plus your Constitution modifier. You can use this feature again by expending one use of your Rage. While you are {@condition Bloodied}, You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Abyss
entries: Encounters with the horrors of the abyssal depths can shatter the minds of the weak, but some transform that trauma into a weapon, forged in the lightless depths where the sun never reaches. The barbarian who follows this path has survived an encounter with the deep and emerged with extraordinary abilities.

subclassFeature.name: Gift of the Drowned
entries: At 3rd level, you gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your walking Speed and can breathe underwater. You also gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage. If you already have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet instead.

subclassFeature.name: Tentacle of Terror
entries: When you enter your Rage, you manifest an unnatural appendage that lasts for the duration of your Rage.

entries.name: Abyssal Lash
entries: As a {@action Bonus Action|XPHB} on your subsequent turns, you can make a melee attack with the appendage against one creature within 15 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes bludgeoning damage equal to {@damage 1d8} + your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Grasp of the Currents
entries: If the Abyssal Lash hits, the target suffers one of the following effects of your choice:

items: {@bold Drag.} The target is pulled up to 10 feet in a straight line toward the appendage.
{@bold Anchor.} The target's Speed is reduced by half until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Phantom Dive
entries: While you are raging, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to teleport to an unoccupied space near a wounded creature within 30 feet of your original position. You then have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against that creature until the end of your next turn or until you make an attack against it.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You can use this feature again by expending one use of your Rage. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Abyssal Gifts
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one of the following benefits. You gain the chosen benefit until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items: {@bold Abyssal Sight.} You gain {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} out to 90 feet. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, its range increases by 60 feet instead. Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you enter your Rage, you gain the benefits of the {@spell True Seeing|XPHB} spell until your Rage ends.
{@bold Abyssal Arms.} When you use your Tentacle of Terror feature, you manifest one additional natural appendage. You can target two different creatures with your Abyssal Lash.

{@bold Heart of the Ocean.} When you enter your Rage, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while your Rage is active, you can gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d12} + your Barbarian level. You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1) per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
{@bold Resolve of the Depths.} You are immune to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions. You also have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

{@bold Armor of the Deep.} Your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} increases by 1. While you are raging, when a creature hits you with a melee attack, it takes Cold damage equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).

entries: At 14th level, you can choose two of these benefits whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Abyssal Charge
entries: When you use your Phantom Dive feature, you can unleash a shockwave at the point where you arrive. Each creature within 10 feet of that point must make a Strength saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d10} Force damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. If you use Phantom Dive to appear in a space containing water, the radius of the explosion increases to 20 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Demon
entries: You were possessed by the spirit of a demon, which bound its soul to yours to empower your fury. This path offers a chance for vengeance: perhaps a demon possessed someone you knew, or you encountered it while exploring an abandoned dungeon, where you touched a cursed object that the demon had sworn to protect even after death.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Within
entries: Your Rage is no longer fueled solely by your own anger, but by the spirit of the demon that possesses you. While you are raging, you can’t be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB}. If you are already affected by either condition when you enter your Rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of your Rage. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire and Necrotic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Endless Hunger
entries: The demon's spirit infuses your weapon with its essence. When you enter your Rage, When you enter your Rage, you can summon the weapon to your hand. and empower it with a sinister glow. The weapon sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius. While the weapon is empowered, it gains the Thrown property with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can summon the weapon back to your hand.

subclassFeature.name: Demon in Me
entries: Once per turn, you can add a number of {@damage d6s} equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded down) to the damage roll of a weapon attack. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. At 14th level, the damage die of this feature increases to a {@damage d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Growing Darkness
entries: The influence of the demon grows stronger within your mortal form. You gain the following benefits.
You can see through magical darkness and ignore the effects of magical silence.

{@bold Infernal Scream.} When you enter your Rage, each creature within 20 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier On a failed save, a creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. This feature ignores any {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Fury
entries: When you enter your Rage, a pair of wings made of blood and flames emerge from your back. You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your Speed. Additionally, you are immune to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} and {@condition Blinded|XPHB} conditions. Finally, at the end of your turn, if you have hit a creature with an attack during that turn, you regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the additional damage dealt by your Demon in Me feature.

subclassFeature.name: College of Tides
entries: The waters of Aetherion are filled with pirates, storms, and sea monsters. Because of this, crews often seek out a Buhru priest, a mad captain, or a one-armed veteran to ensure a safe voyage. Those who have studied the sea, whether through formal training or firsthand experience, are invaluable when navigating such dangers.

subclassFeature.name: Boarding
entries: When you grant a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, that creature's Speed increases by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature expends that die on an attack roll and the attack hits, the creature can immediately move up to 5 feet. This movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

subclassFeature.name: Sea Shanties
entries: You have learned the sea shanties passed down among the sailors of Aetherion, using their rhythms to inspire courage and coordination among your allies. As a {@action Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to give a Bardic Inspiration die to a number of creatures of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of yourself, up to a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). A creature must be able to hear you to receive this die. You can have a number of Bardic Inspiration dice granted by this feature at the same time equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). If you grant a Bardic Inspiration die to a creature while you already have the maximum number of dice granted by this feature, the oldest Bardic Inspiration die granted by this feature disappears.

subclassFeature.name: Crew Member
entries: You gain proficiency with Water Vehicles and Navigator's Tools. If you already have proficiency with either, you gain Expertise instead. You also learn one of the following languages: Aquan or Buhru.

{@bold Crew's Mockery.} You learn the {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} cantrip. If you already know this cantrip, you learn another {@filter cantrip from the Bard spell list|spells|level=0|class=Bard}. When a creature within 60 feet of you misses you or one of your allies with an attack roll, you can cast {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} as a {@action Reaction|XPHB} targeting that creature. When you cast the spell in this way, you can add your Bardic Inspiration die to the spell's damage roll if the ally targeted by the attack has one of your Bardic Inspiration dice. The Bardic Inspiration die is then expended.

subclassFeature.name: Broadside
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can take a {@action Bonus Action|XPHB} to coordinate a devastating volley. Each allied creature within 60 feet of you that has one of your Bardic Inspiration dice can use its {@action Reaction|XPHB} to make one weapon attack or one spell attack against the same target. These attacks are resolved in initiative order, starting with the highest initiative. Each ally that makes an attack in this way expends its Bardic Inspiration die. For each of these attacks that hits after the first, the total damage dealt by this feature increases by an additional {@damage 1d8}. Roll all additional damage dice together and apply the total to the last attack that hits as part of the Broadside. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: College of Temptation
entries: Temptation is the song of vice and wickedness, and the Bards of the College of Temptation wield its melody to indulge their darkest desires. Born of seduction, the Bards of this college are masters of enchantment and deception, manipulating others like puppets in a cruel and twisted game.

subclassFeature.name: Beguiling Presence
entries: You always have {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} prepared. It doesn't count against the number of spells you have prepared. Starting at 7th level, you also always have {@spell Charm Monster|XPHB} prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you have prepared. In addition, your enchantment magic is infused with corruptive allure. While a creature is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you, it gains the following effects:

items: It can't willingly use its movement to end its turn farther away from you than it started, provided it can see or hear you.
It has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom (Perception) checks while it can see or hear you.
Once on each of your turns, when you deal damage to it, it takes extra Psychic damage equal to the die of your Bardic Inspiration.

subclassFeature.name: Succubus's Kiss
entries: You can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to cast {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. When you cast the spell this way, it gains the following benefits:

items: The target doesn't have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its saving throw for being in combat with you.

You can ignore either the spell's Verbal or Somatic component (but not both). The remaining component must take the form of a flirtatious gesture or affectionate words, such as a blown kiss or whispered compliment.
If the target fails its saving throw by 5 or more, it doesn't realize it was charmed by the spell when the spell ends.

entries: Starting at 7th level, you can use this feature to cast {@spell Charm Monster|XPHB} instead of {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Cruel Affection
entries: Your charm is not broken easily, even when your victims realize your true nature. When you deal damage to a creature {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you, and that damage would normally end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition or the effect causing it, the creature must repeat its saving throw with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. On a failed save, the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition remains in effect. In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you.

subclassFeature.name: Sweet Revenge
entries: You draw power from those who fall under your influence. When a creature {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or dies, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your Bard level (rounded down) + your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Seduction
entries: Starting at 14th level, your allure and cruelty rival those of a true succubus. When you cast {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} using your Succubus's Kiss feature, the spell is cast as though using a 3rd-level spell slot, without expending a spell slot of that level. In addition, when a creature repeats its saving throw against your Cruel Devotion feature after taking damage from you, it doesn't make that saving throw with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
Finally, creatures can't gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells granted by this subclass.

subclassFeature.name: Spirits Domain
entries: It is the will of the Great Kraken and Goddess of Motion, Nagakabouros, that her people endlessly pursue their desires. To her, the greatest sin is stagnation. For this reason, she grants her most devoted followers the honor of speaking in her name and the divine power to test the strength of the spirit. Spirits that remain in motion are spared; those that stagnate receive no mercy.

subclassFeature.name: Spirits Domain Spells
entries: When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Spirits Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.
In addition, you can cast the spells from this feature while you're in a Wild Shape form.

entries.caption: Spirits Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Zone of Truth|XPHB}, {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB}, {@spell Bane|XPHB}, {@spell Bless|XPHB}
{@spell Evard's Black Tentacles|XPHB}, {@spell Guardian of Faith|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Spiritual Rend
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to tear a fragment of spirit from a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself.

The fragment appears in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of the creature and lasts for 1 minute. The effect ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or if the creature is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
The spirit can be targeted and uses the same statistics as the creature, with the following exceptions:

items: The spirit can't be moved or destroyed.
This feature can't be used on Undead or Constructs.

entries: When you attack the spirit, half the damage dealt to it is instead dealt to the original creature.

Whenever the spirit takes damage, the creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a successful save, the effect ends immediately. The creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this saving throw if it is more than 15 feet away from its spirit.
When this effect ends for any reason, the creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Slam
entries: As an {@action Attack|XPHB|Attack Action}, you raise your {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}, causing an illusory tentacle to emerge from it, which you slam into the ground.

Each creature in a 15-foot line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your cleric spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 1d6} + your Wisdom modifier bludgeoning damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).

subclassFeature.name: Free the Soul
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB|Magic Action}, you raise your {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB} to free the spirits of nearby allies, granting up to six creatures of your choice within 60 feet of yourself the effects of {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

In addition, when you use Spiritual Rend, two illusory tentacles appear around the spirit fragment. At the end of your turn, these tentacles attack the spirit fragment, dealing {@damage 1d10} Force damage. This damage ignores the damage reduction from Spiritual Rend.
Whenever a creature hits you with an attack, you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + half the damage taken (rounded down), or one of the tentacles disappears.

subclassFeature.name: Trial of the Spirit
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB|Magic Action}, you raise your {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB} toward the sky.
Each hostile creature of your choice within 60 feet of yourself sees a fragment of its spirit torn from its body, as if you had used your Spiritual Rend feature.
In addition, the damage dealt by the tentacles from your Free the Soul feature increases to {@damage 1d12} Force damage.

subclassFeature.name: Frost Domain
entries: Clerics of the Frost believe that ice represents balance: a force that halts chaos and grants the world the time it needs to heal. They revere the cold because it preserves life rather than consuming it, slowing that which burns too quickly. They preserve existence not to prevent its end, but to ensure that every death is followed by rebirth, like the eternal cycle of Anivia.

subclassFeature.name: Frost Domain Spells
entries: When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Frost Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.
In addition, you can cast the spells from this feature while you're in a Wild Shape form.

entries.caption: Frost Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Ice Knife|XPHB}, {@spell Ray of Enfeeblement|XPHB}, {@spell Frost Fingers|IDRotF}, {@spell Blur|XPHB},

subclassFeature.name: Polar Soul
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is targeted by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to create a wall of ice to protect it. The protected creature gains a bonus to its {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB|AC} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} until the end of your next turn. You must use this feature before knowing whether the attack roll hits or misses. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).

subclassFeature.name: Relentless Winter
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to unleash an aura of supernatural frost. As a {@action Magic|XPHB|Magic Action}, you present your {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}. Each hostile creature within 15 feet of yourself must make a Constitution saving throw against your cleric spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} for 1 minute as ice freezes around its lower limbs. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. On a successful save, a creature's Speed is halved while it remains in the area. At the end of each of your turns, creatures affected by the frost take {@damage 1d4} + your Wisdom modifier cold damage.

subclassFeature.name: Frozen Touch
entries: When a creature within 30 feet of yourself that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 2d8} cold damage, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
